subject: Measurement error for exposure variable in Poisson Lognormal model

messages.author: 5bc0b352c8d95b37
messages.subject: Measurement error for exposure variable in Poisson Lognormal model
parts:
Dear all, I'm trying to create a Poisson log-normal model for car crashes counts and I just started reading the documentation and papers on the Measurement error models (Muff et al., 2015). I was wondering if it's possible (and if it does make sense) to apply the measurement error approach to the exposure component (E) of the PLN model. If so, could you suggest me some examples and code?

Kind regards
Andrea

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Measurement error for exposure variable in Poisson Lognormal model
parts:
You can always do similar things, but instead if 'E' you can play with
the offset, like

y ~ 1 + offset(log(E)) + ...


well, what you can do is to add a me model around that one, where you
have to be careful about priors in order to get anything useful.

this is 'almost' the same as adding a iid random effect on top of the
offset.
